home.title: Catch3: C++ testing beyond assertions
home.description: Catch3 keeps the tests you write for Catch2 and adds a runner of its own, property tests, mocks, snapshots and structured results. C++17.
home.headline: C++ testing beyond assertions.
home.lede: Catch3 keeps the test cases, assertions and sections you write for Catch2, and adds a runner of its own, property tests, mocks, snapshots and structured results.
home.field: A field of tests in perspective: a wave turns them green, one turns red, is caught and turns green.
home.featuresLede: Everything Catch2 tests do keeps working. What Catch3 adds is beside it, in its own headers and its own library.

authoring.title: Familiar tests
authoring.text: Test cases, assertions, sections, matchers, generators, listeners and benchmarks keep working unchanged.

runner.title: A runner of its own
runner.text: Tests run in parallel worker processes; a crash or a hang ends one test, not the run. Failures are retried to tell flaky and order-dependent tests apart.

history.title: A run remembers
history.text: History drives time limits, ordering, incremental runs and replay. Flaky tests go to quarantine; reports come out as console, JUnit, JSON and traces.

properties.title: Property tests
properties.text: Values come from a reproducible seed, a predicate is checked over many trials, and a failing input shrinks to a smaller counterexample.

mocks.title: Mocks
mocks.text: Mocks of virtual interfaces and of free functions behind a seam check call counts, arguments and order.

snapshots.title: Snapshots and results
snapshots.text: Text snapshots in files you choose, and a public result model with a deterministic JUnit XML writer.

home.exampleTitle: A property in a few lines
home.exampleText: The root seed and the derivation of each trial are stable, so a failing trial that is reported can be replayed.
home.buildsText: Bazel is the main build. CMake, Meson, Xmake and Premake project files are kept beside it, and an installed Catch3 is found with find_package or pkg-config.
home.licenseText: Files that come from Catch2 keep the Boost Software License 1.0; files Progmasoft writes are under the GNU LGPL, version 3 or later. Catch3 is not an official Catch2 release and is not endorsed by Catch2's maintainers.
home.ctaText: Download the library, read how a Catch2 project moves over, and run your first property.

download.title: Download Catch3
download.description: Install the catch3 command on Linux, macOS or Windows, or use the Catch3 library from source.
download.lede: Choose your system. The page shows how to install the catch3 command there.

requirements.linux: Linux with glibc 2.28 or later, on x86-64 or ARM64.
requirements.macos: macOS 13 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.
requirements.windows: Windows 10 or later, 64-bit, on x64 or ARM64.

download.notice: Catch3 {version}, the latest release, has no catch3 command; the installers below fetch it from the first release that has one. The library below is in every release.
download.commandText: catch3 reads test results and reports them, imports the results of other test frameworks and runs test binaries. It carries its C++ standard library inside, so it asks nothing of the system's libstdc++.

download.macosRun: Download the installer of the release and run it:
download.optionUser: Without options the script installs for the current user.
download.optionGlobal: installs for every user of the machine
download.caseZsh: The options of install.zsh tell upper and lower case apart.
download.caseCmd: The options of install.cmd tell upper and lower case apart, except /HELP.
download.casePowerShell: The options of Install-Catch3.ps1 do not tell upper and lower case apart.
download.verify: A script downloads the archive for your processor with curl and checks it against its SHA-256 file, and against its BLAKE3 file when b3sum is installed. A mismatch stops it before anything is extracted; it then extracts into a temporary directory and installs from there.
